📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

📣 Bitcoin price has reclaimed the $80,000 level after briefly falling below it earlier on Thursday, as fresh US economic data showed stronger than expected growth in the third quarter and persistent inflation in September. The latest figures arrived a day after the Federal Reserve decided to leave interest rates unchanged, raising fresh questions about whether the central bank could consider another rate hike before the end of the year.

⚠️ Bitcoin (BTC) had dropped to approximately $79,800 earlier in the session before recovering above $80,000. However, the cryptocurrency remained under pressure following Wednesday’s Fed decision, with traders assessing how the latest economic figures could affect monetary policy. Thursday’s advance GDP estimate showed that the US economy grew faster in the third quarter, supported mainly by consumer spending, business investment, and government expenditure.

🌐 Business investment remained another contributor, particularly as technology companies continued spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure and equipment. However, the stronger economic performance was accompanied by inflation figures that showed consumer prices continued to rise in September. A failure without a traitor

A secret traitor would give some in Israel a convenient explanation for Oct. 7. The country’s former military chief offers something harder to dismiss. The institutions failed at their jobs.

“October 7 was a failure that could have been prevented, but there was absolutely no internal betrayal,” 
former IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi told a Shurat HaDin conference in New York on Sunday.

A conspiracy capable of enabling the attack would require a broad network, he said, and after three years not one collaborator has been found.

Halevi described a mistaken assessment, shared by the military, the Shin Bet and the political leadership, that Hamas did not want war. Israel ranked Iran first, Hezbollah second and Hamas third. Hamas worked hard to reinforce that assessment. The deception succeeded across institutions responsible for detecting it.

Halevi also defended military pressure as necessary to bring hostages home, while acknowledging its lethal consequences.
 “Our own bombs killed hostages. Of course, this was not intentional. We did not know they were there,” 
he said.
He called for a full inquiry and recalled the photograph of Shiri Bibas, who was abducted with her two young sons and killed in Hamas captivity. 
“We were not there in time to help and save her. That is the failure,” 
he said.

Halevi commanded the army when that failure occurred. His account belongs before an inquiry, alongside the decisions of the political leadership. Hunting an imaginary traitor would be considerably easier than questioning the actual people in charge.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round. Fortune reported that the company previously raised $5 million in seed financing in 2022, followed by additional capital from existing backers.
